lesson.text: Quick memory: what are the small tiles of a mosaic called? (Tesserae.) Today: art from around the world, from 500 to 1500.
In monasteries, monks copied books by hand on parchment. They illuminated them: big decorated capitals, bright colours and real gold that catches the light. The Book of Kells was made around 800.
Their paints came from nature: blue from a stone called lapis lazuli, carried all the way from Afghanistan; red from minerals; ink from oak galls. They wrote with quill pens made from feathers.

Islamic artists covered mosques and palaces with geometric patterns, flowing plants and beautiful writing, drawn with just a compass and a ruler. The Alhambra palace in Spain (1300s) is famous for them.

In the Kingdom of Benin, in today's Nigeria, skilled casters made brass heads and plaques for the Oba, the king. They made them from about the 1200s, by the lost-wax method. Benin City's casters still work today.
Lost-wax casting: model the shape in wax over a clay core, and cover it in clay. Heat it so the wax melts out, and pour hot metal into the gap. Then break the mould to free the metal shape.

In China, Song dynasty painters (960-1279) painted mountains and water in ink: shan shui, mountain-water. Mist is left as empty paper, far hills are pale, and a tiny traveller shows how vast nature is.
Try it in the world: design an illuminated first letter of your name with a border of vines. Or build a tiled floor with an eight-pointed star in your world. Next: geometric patterns.

exercises.hint: Illuminate means light up. What lit up the pages?
choices: a hand-made book with colour and gold
a book with a lamp inside
exercises.explain: It is a book copied by hand and lit up with bright colours and real gold.

exercises.prompt: Monks in Europe copied books by hand because there were no printing presses there yet.
exercises.explain: True: before printing, every book was copied by hand.

exercises.prompt: What kind of Chinese painting is this?
exercises.hint: Mountains, mist and water in ink.
exercises.explain: It is shan shui, mountain-water painting, in ink on a scroll.

exercises.prompt: Where would you see a pattern like this eight-pointed star?
exercises.hint: Geometry drawn with a compass and ruler.
exercises.explain: Eight-pointed stars are found on Islamic tiles, as at the Alhambra.

exercises.prompt: Match each art to where it was made.
exercises.hint: Monks, the Oba, ink mountains and a palace in Spain.
exercises.explain: Illuminated books came from monasteries, brass heads from Benin, shan shui from Song China and tiled geometry from the Alhambra.

exercises.prompt: Put the steps of lost-wax casting in order.
exercises.hint: The wax must be gone before the metal goes in.
items: heat it so the wax melts out
exercises.explain: Wax model, clay coat, melt the wax out, pour the metal, break the mould.

exercises.prompt: Label the Chinese landscape: tap a word, then its number.
exercises.hint: Far things are pale and high up; mist is the empty band; the traveller is tiny.
exercises.explain: Pale peaks at the top are the far mountains, the empty band is mist, the dark slopes are the near mountains and the tiny figure is the traveller.

exercises.prompt: Why are the far mountains in shan shui painted pale?
exercises.hint: Think of hills on a misty day.
exercises.explain: Far-away things look paler, so pale ink makes them seem far.

exercises.prompt: Islamic geometric patterns were drawn with just a compass and a ruler.
exercises.hint: Think of the eight dots on a circle.
exercises.explain: True: circles and straight lines build every star and tile.

exercises.prompt: Where did the blue for illuminated books often come from?
exercises.hint: It was precious, carried very far.
choices: lapis lazuli, a stone from Afghanistan
exercises.explain: Lapis lazuli, ground into powder, came all the way from Afghanistan.

exercises.prompt: The Book of Kells was made around the year 800. How many years is it from 800 to 2026?
exercises.hint: Take the smaller year away from the bigger one.

exercises.prompt: How is this eight-pointed star built?
exercises.hint: Join every second point on the circle.
choices: from a triangle and a circle
exercises.explain: Joining every second point makes two squares, one turned 45°.

exercises.prompt: The Benin plaques were carved from wood.
exercises.hint: What did the casters pour into their moulds?
exercises.explain: False: they were cast in brass with the lost-wax method.

exercises.prompt: In shan shui painting, what does the tiny traveller show?
exercises.hint: Compare the traveller with the mountains.
choices: how vast nature is next to people
exercises.explain: The tiny figure makes the mountains feel huge: people are small in nature.

exercises.prompt: Put these artworks in time order, oldest first.
What does illuminated mean for these books?
exercises.hint: What catches the light on the page?
choices: lit up with gold and bright colour
exercises.explain: The gold and bright colours make the page seem to glow with light.

exercises.prompt: A monk copies one page a day, every day. How many weeks does a 350-page book take?
exercises.hint: How many pages in one week?
exercises.explain: 7 pages a week, and 350 ÷ 7 = 50 weeks: nearly a year.
